cuts.reason: §7a religion and religious practice. Britannica (checked 2026-11-10) describes an unofficial cease-fire on 24–25 December 1914, Christmas trees, the hymn Stille Nacht, answering carols, and an appeal from Pope Benedict XV. The story cannot be told without that religious day. Football and gifts do not save it. Cut, not softened.

§7a plus the no-invented-facts rule. The draft quote 'I miss you' had no primary source. A US museum letter page and a British evacuation were mixed into one child. The draft said about 1.5 million civilians, 'the overwhelming majority' children, in three days. The UK government history blog (30 Aug 2019) says over 1.5 million people, of whom 800,000 were children. A BBC History page says nearly 3 million people in four days. The counts conflict, so none is taught. The folktale codename is omitted (mythology is out). The sourced morning is kept as school-morning, not as this draft.

facts.text: On 1 September 1939 the government began the evacuation. Children of Myrdle School in Stepney assembled at school at 5am that Friday. The same start moved over 1.5 million people from urban target areas, of whom 800,000 were children, including from Manchester, Birmingham, and Glasgow, not only London.

notTaught: No count of people or children. A BBC History page says nearly 3 million people in the first four days (https://www.bbc.com/history/british/britain_wwtwo/evacuees_01.shtml). That conflicts with the government blog's over 1.5 million people, of whom 800,000 were children. Neither number is said to the child.
No letter text. 'I miss you' was not sourced. A museum catalogue of letters from a Canada evacuation is a different journey and is not used.
No folktale codename, gas masks, bombs, soldiers, or a nation named as an enemy.
No kilometers. No train on this street: the blog says they assembled at the school at 5am. A photograph shows a walk with cases. It does not show a train here, so the clip does not.

facts.text: The armistice was signed at 5:45 am on 11 November 1918 at Compiègne, France, and took effect at 11:00 am, ending the war on the Western Front.

notTaught: The 5:45 signing time is a source fact and is not asked. The narration teaches 11 in the morning, when it went quiet.
No who-won line, no signing table, no flags, no soldiers, no guns, no poppies, no monument. Poppies and stone memorials stay with the monuments journal.
